# Draft:Gopreksheshwar

----
Mokshling Shree Gopreksheshwar Mahadev (Ardhnarishwar)
Gopreksheshwar (also known as Gauri Shankar) is an ancient and sacred Shiva Lingam located in Varanasi (Kashi). Its significance is primarily rooted in Ling Puran, In Padm Puran, In Narad Puran and in , where it is hailed for its ability to grant the spiritual merit of cow donation and resolve domestic conflicts.
Religious & Mythological Significance
Merit of Cow Donation (Godaan): According to the Skanda Purana, worshipping or even catching a glimpse of the Gopreksheshwar Lingam provides a devotee with the same spiritual benefits as donating an infinite number of cows (Godaan) to deserving persons
The Legend of the Celestial Cows: The name "Gopreksheshwar" is derived from a legend where  Lord Shiva ordered cows from the celestial realm (Goloka) to go to Kashi. When they arrived, Shiva appeared before them with Goddess Parvati (Gauri) to grant them his vision (Darshan). Because he gave Darshan to the cows (Go), the site became known as Gopreksheshwar.
Ardhanarishwar Form: It is a unique manifestation of Shiva and Shakti together. In this shrine, Lord Shiva resides in the form of the Lingam, while Mother Gauri is present as an idol (Vigraha) within the same structure, representing the unified masculine and feminine powers.
Resolution of Conflicts: Devotees believe that worshipping at this shrine destroys all sins (Kalmash) and specifically resolves marital or domestic disputes (Dampatya Klesh).)
